threat_assessment:
The table has you filed before you untap. Five colours plus a legendary tutor reads as archenemy to anybody who has ever lost to one, and four Game Changers named in the pregame seals it. Let them file it. They are watching your commander, and your commander is not the threshold.

Look at what they are actually pointing at. With no other legend out, Sisay is a 2/2 whose gate reads "cheaper than two", and this list runs no legendary lands to sit at the bottom of that gate. Three cards are legal there and one of them adds no colour. So never activate into a cold board — put a colour-diverse legend down first and fire next turn.

Count colours among your other legends, never mana. One colour opens ten targets and two opens twenty-three, so spend the whole early game buying that second colour: it is thirteen cards of access on one drop. Three opens twenty-eight and four opens all thirty-three.

Then stop climbing. Nothing in this deck costs more than five mana, so four colours is the ceiling and the fifth buys stats you did not need. Spend that turn holding protection instead of chasing a rung that pays nothing.

She arrives by turn three in ninety-five games out of a hundred, so stop treating her as the thing you are building toward — she is the thing you build from. The five-colour source lands beside her by turn six a little over half the time. Set your pivot at turn five or six and play everything before it as setup you are happy with, not as delay you are apologising for.

Four things flip you from ignored to archenemy. Five untapped colour sources sitting next to Sisay. An omni-mana body resolving — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, the cards that visibly solve a five-pip bill. Najeela. And a second activation inside one turn cycle, which ends the conversation entirely.

Choose which of those you show and on which turn. Do not let the draw order choose for you.

Sequence your colours onto bodies nobody fears. Katilda, Kutzil, Kinnan, Lotho, Kambal and Saffi each buy two rungs on a card that looks like a draft creature. Lead with those and leave Najeela and Jodah in the library, where they are safe and still yours.

Do not bluff with open mana. Visible WUBRG taxes the table's plays, but it advertises interaction you structurally do not have: every counterspell and both free protection instants are non-legendary, part of the twenty-six cards Sisay can never reach. If you are holding something real, hold it. If you are not, tap out behind a modest permanent and look poorer than you are.

Here is the asymmetry almost nobody else at the table gets. Your scariest cards live in your library and you can reach them at will, so you never need Najeela in hand and never have to look like you have her. Play the whole midgame as a fair legends deck. Time the tell for the turn it wins rather than the turn it impresses.

Rhystic Study is the exception and the trap. It is a Game Changer and it is non-legendary — a card you drew rather than a card you chose — and it will make you the archenemy faster than anything Sisay can find. At a table still deciding who to hit, sit on it.

Now learn how the good pilots kill you, because it changes your sequencing today. They do not spend removal on Sisay; they kill the rung — the single legend that is your only source of a colour, in response to the activation, so the fetch shrinks under you. Audit that every turn: which colour is single-sourced right now? Deploy the redundant colour before the greedy fetch, and the moment Shalai is legal, go get her.

A sweeper is the other way you die, and it charges you twice: the board, and the ladder from twenty-eight targets back to three. That one has its own instructions below.

Embrace the label when three things land together — three colours among your other legends, the five pips genuinely payable, and either protection up or Kutzil holding your window open. Take the archenemy seat then, on your turn, on purpose. Until that turn, be the fourth-most-interesting board at the table and enjoy it. You know exactly what you are building toward and they are guessing.

One thing to leave open on purpose. Whether a legend you just fetched can help pay for the next activation on the same turn is not settled here — the resolution that asked the question did not clear the checker. Plan on one activation per turn cycle. If it turns out you chain, that is a gift, not a plan.
matchups:
Sweeper control. Assume the wrath — across four players one is close to certain — and price it correctly, because against you it takes the board and drops the ladder from twenty-eight targets to three. So keep a two-colour legend in hand rather than on board. Katilda, Kutzil, Kinnan, Lotho, Kambal, Saffi: the hand copy rebuilds two rungs after the wipe, the board copy dies with everything else.

Know which of your saves actually save. Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention and Boros Charm's indestructible mode beat destruction wraths and do nothing at all against exile or against a -X/-X like your own Toxic Deluge. Protection is available by turn six in eighty games out of a hundred, so fetch into that number rather than sandbagging for a save you probably already hold.

Deluge is your permission slip. You recover from a wipe cheaper than anyone at the table, so pick the timing yourself instead of letting the control seat pick it. Rebuild worst threat first, and count the extra two mana each trip through the command zone charges you before you promise yourself a recast.

Stax and tax. You are the beatdown here and you do not get to argue about it — race the lock's completion, because you never own the long game underneath one. Five coloured pips with zero generic, activated repeatedly, is the most tax-exposed shape in the format; there is nothing generic to pay around. Recount your activations under the tax, not your cards.

Recount honestly, because three of your own accelerants quit on you here. Delighted Halfling makes mana for legendary spells and an activation is not a spell, Unclaimed Territory is creature spells only, and Sol Ring is colourless against five colours. Plaza of Heroes carries the same trap with an escape — the any-colour mode pays fine — and Secluded Courtyard named on Human pays because its own clause says "or activate an ability". Read the clause, then count the source.

Name your out before you go get it. Loran of the Third Path is three mana, live from two colours, and destroys the artifact or enchantment on the way in; Teferi's bounce is the backup. Fetch the piece locking you, not the scariest piece on the table.

Aggro. You are behind roughly 120 life spread across three defences, so do not race — nobody is asking you to. Buy virtual answers instead of spending real ones: Thalia makes their creatures and nonbasics enter tapped, Sheoldred bills them two life a draw, Shalai hands you and your creatures hexproof, Flowering turns your small legends into warded blockers. All four are legendary at two to four mana, so all four are one activation away from two colours onward.

That is the whole trick against three attackers. One fetch that blanks plans at three seats beats one removal spell that answers one card. If a single seat drags you into a race, treat it as a subgame, spend the minimum that wins it, and keep your eyes on the other two.

Combo. Invert everything. Hold the pips for interaction and count the table's open mana instead of climbing, because a wide gate is worth nothing if the game ends before you walk through it. Your one Path to Exile is worth most the moment the piece hits the battlefield — spend it there, not on the turn you finally feel safe.

The structural problem is that your interaction is exactly what Sisay cannot see. Every counterspell, Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver, Drannith Magistrate and Grand Abolisher sit inside the twenty-six cards outside her reach, so fetch disruption rather than a finisher. Teferi at three mana pushes them to sorcery speed and Kutzil switches their spells off during your turn. Take either over Najeela for as long as a combo deck is alive.

Fair value midrange. Here you are cleanly the control seat, so slow the game down and stop hunting for action. Picture turn fifteen with everybody on their best draws — you like that picture, which means your job is making the game reach it. Look boring for a turn or two after every visible fetch and sequence Najeela and Jodah last.

Graveyard hate. Mostly a blank against you, and every Bojuka Bog pointed here instead of at the reanimator seat is a card you got for free — say nothing and let them spend it. Do not build a plan on your own yard either: Saffi's sacrifice trigger is the entire recursion suite. Keep Dauthi Voidwalker for those decks, and remember that like everything else non-legendary, he only ever arrives by draw.

Every archetype above ends at the same instruction. Fetch the card that changes what the table is allowed to do, and leave the card that ends the game in the library until the turn it ends it.

The only line here that has been walked through the rules and survived an adversarial check is Najeela with Derevi, and it wants a mana base producing all five colours every combat — build toward that, not toward the nine unresolved lines the combo data flags. Stumble into those. Never keep a hand for them.

cover.tagline: The tutor that widens every time it fires - and the five-pip bill that comes due every time.
cover.identity: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain is a repeatable battlefield tutor whose reach is bought in colours: she is a 2/2 plus one for each colour among your other legendary permanents, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} searches out any legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power. That makes this an access curve rather than a card curve - 3 legal targets at power 2, then 10, 23, 28 and 33 as the board picks up colours - funded by 40 lands and a small battery of bodies that can produce five distinct coloured pips at once. It is a bracket 4 (Optimized) list on contents alone: four Game Changers put the floor there independently of any combo line, and the Najeela combat loop is the closer.

how_it_wins:
The table looks at five colours and files you under greedy. Let them. What you actually brought is a fair tutor that never taps, never says once per turn, and gets better every time it fires — and access is the only currency this deck spends.

Read her power, not her mana cost. Sisay is a 2/2 plus one for every colour among your other legendary permanents, and she finds any legendary permanent cheaper than that power. Three legal targets at power 2, ten at power 3, twenty-three at power 4. So your first move is never "cast Sisay" — it is "put a colour-dense legend down before you activate." Derevi buys three rungs for three mana. Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho, Saffi, Kambal and Kutzil each buy two.

Stop climbing at four colours. Nothing in this list costs more than five mana, so power 6 already opens all 33 targets and the fifth colour buys stats and Jodah's anthem and zero new access. Spend that turn holding up protection instead.

Here is the trap that eats new pilots. Most of what looks like acceleration cannot pay her: Sol Ring makes colourless, Delighted Halfling's any-colour mana is for legendary spells only and an activation is not a spell, Unclaimed Territory is creature spells only. Use those to deploy her, then count the six cards that genuinely foot the bill — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends, Selvala — alongside Command Tower, Arcane Signet, Plaza of Heroes and Secluded Courtyard named on Human.

She is on the board by turn three in 95 games out of 100, so never plan around finding her. Plan around the turn she and a five-colour source arrive together, which happens by turn six a little over half the time. That is the turn your deck starts existing.

Then go shopping for the answer instead of holding it. This list runs one unconditional creature removal spell and one sweeper, and it does not need more, because Kutzil and Teferi take away the windows in which opponents may act, Thalia makes their board and their lands arrive tapped, and Kambal and Sheoldred bill them for their own turns. All of them are legendary at mana value 2 to 4 — pick the tax that hurts the seat that is actually beating you and go get it.

Watch which colour finishes your ladder. Among your other 33 legendary permanents, white appears on 19 and green on 14, but blue on 8, red on 6 and black on 5 — and the only red legend at three mana or less is Najeela. The card that completes your fourth colour and the card that makes you the archenemy are frequently the same card, so fetch her with the mana up to use her.

The kill is that Najeela, and it is the one line here that has been walked against the Comprehensive Rules and cleared an adversarial check: a deterministic, unbounded combat loop with Derevi that ends the table. Nine other lines the combo data flags for this deck are unresolved. Treat them as board states you might stumble into, never as the plan you keep a hand for.

Know your one real weakness and play around it on purpose. Twenty-six of your nonland cards are not legendary and are invisible to her forever — three of the six cards that pay her bill, every counterspell, both free protection instants, and all four Game Changers. She finds payoffs. You have to draw the fuel.

card_roles.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: Count colours before you count mana: her power is 2 plus one per colour among your other legendary permanents, and she finds anything cheaper than that. No tap symbol and no once-per-turn clause, so the only cap on her is how often you can produce {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.
card_roles.An Offer You Can't Refuse: One blue to stop the wrath or the removal aimed at your ladder. The two Treasures you hand back are cheaper than rebuilding, and they rarely make the colour that matters to them.
card_roles.Arcane Denial: Two mana to keep an activation alive, and you replace the card on the next upkeep. Point it at whatever would cost you the most rungs.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour in the identity for two mana, which makes it one of the few rocks that pays a real pip of her cost. Play it ahead of a three-drop, not after.
card_roles.Birds of Paradise: Turn-one Birds is a turn-two commander and a permanent pip of any colour. Protect it like a land in the early turns — it is your fifth colour more often than a land is.
card_roles.Bloom Tender: One mana per colour on your board, scaling off exactly the same colours the ladder counts, so it grows as you climb. It is non-legendary, so you will never fetch it — keep it when it shows up in an opener.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Your cheapest full-board save against a sweeper, and a 4-damage burn spell when nobody is threatening. Decide the mode after they commit, not before.
card_roles.Bristly Bill, Spine Sower: Two mana for a green rung on the ladder, with counters arriving off every land drop. Play it for the colour and take the counters as change.
card_roles.Dauthi Voidwalker: The hardest cost in the deck at double black on turn two, and the reason your black source count is stressed — cast it on a turn black is comfortable. It blanks graveyard decks and steals their best card on the way out.
card_roles.Delighted Halfling: Deploys the commander a turn early and pays nothing toward what she does next: its coloured mana is for legendary spells only, and an activation is not a spell. Use it to cast, never to count.
card_roles.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: Three colours on one three-mana body — the single best rung you can buy — and the other half of the verified kill. Her combat-damage trigger taps or untaps a permanent for every creature that connects, so an attack refills your lands.
card_roles.Dihada, Binder of Wills: Four mana, three colours, and a +2 that hands your commander indestructible until your next turn. Use the plus far more often than you dig with the minus.
card_roles.Dispel: One mana held for the instant aimed at Sisay while an activation sits on the stack. Keep it up on the turn you plan to fire, not the turn you plan to fetch.
card_roles.Drannith Magistrate: Two mana that turns off every command zone at the table, including the recursion your removal-heavy opponents rely on. Assume it eats the next removal spell and be glad it did.
card_roles.Emiel the Blessed: Three mana per blink, and it dodges targeted removal as well as it re-buys an enter-the-battlefield trigger. Hold the mana on turns you expect an answer.
card_roles.Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic: Its front face is a green rung that taps for any colour and gives every other legendary creature you control the same ability — the board becomes the battery. Fetch it as soon as you have bodies to arm.
card_roles.Esper Sentinel: Turn one, every time. It taxes the first noncreature spell each opponent casts, which in a pod of three is a card a turn cycle unless everyone pays you.
card_roles.Faeburrow Elder: It pays a pip of every colour on your board and grows as the ladder does, so treat it as a second Bloom Tender. Non-legendary again — draw it, or do without it.
card_roles.Fellwar Stone: Two mana that copies what the table's lands can make, which in a four-player pod is usually the colour you are missing. Cast it early and check what it makes before you plan the turn.
card_roles.Fierce Guardianship: Free with your commander out, so it costs you nothing to hold up on the turn you commit. Save it for the wrath or the targeted answer, not for a value spell.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free while she is on the battlefield, and it keeps the whole board through a sweeper. This is the card that makes committing a fourth legend safe.
card_roles.Flowering of the White Tree: Ward on the legends means every removal spell aimed at your ladder costs an extra mana, and the +2/+1 turns your utility bodies into a clock. Fetch it when the table is holding cheap interaction.
card_roles.Grand Abolisher: On your turn opponents cannot cast spells at all, or activate their artifacts, creatures and enchantments — activate through their counterspells and removal freely. Deploy him before the big turn, not during it.
card_roles.Heliod, Sun-Crowned: A three-mana white rung that counts for the ladder whether or not devotion makes it a creature. The lifelink grant turns any body into a life swing when the race is on.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Two mana that answers a sweeper and a targeted spell alike, and it covers your mana creatures as well as your legends. Hold it whenever you tap low.
card_roles.Ioreth of the Healing House: Untap two other legendary creatures and the battery pays twice in one turn — that is a second activation out of a board you already have. Point it at whichever two produce the most colours.
card_roles.Jegantha, the Wellspring: One tap for {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, which is exactly the bill and nothing else, since that mana cannot pay generic costs. Once it can tap, a single card funds a whole activation.
card_roles.Jodah, the Unifier: Five mana, so he needs four colours on the ladder before she can find him. He pays back with an anthem that makes your utility legends lethal and free casts off the top.
card_roles.Kambal, Consul of Allocation: Two colours on a three-mana body, and every noncreature spell the table casts drains them for two. Fetch him against decks that win with spells rather than bodies.
card_roles.Katilda, Dawnhart Prime: Two mana for two rungs, and it hands every Human you control a mana ability — including Sisay, whose activation has no tap symbol, so once she is settled she helps pay for herself.
card_roles.Kenrith, the Returned King: Five activated abilities across all five colours: the mana sink for turns where the ladder has topped out and you still have mana. Trample and haste is the mode that ends games.
card_roles.Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy: Two mana, two rungs, and every nonland tap for mana gets an extra mana of a type it made — that is a whole extra colour off Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder. Deploy it before the battery, not after.
card_roles.Kodama of the West Tree: A three-mana green rung whose land ramp triggers off the counters your own deck hands out. Take it when you need green on board and a body that connects.
card_roles.Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar: Opponents cannot cast spells during your turn, which is the cheapest protection an activation will ever get. Fetch it before the turn you intend to go off, not on it.
card_roles.Loran of the Third Path: The one artifact-and-enchantment answer the tutor can actually go and get, so hold the fetch until you see the lock piece or the stax rock. The draw ability is a bonus you will rarely have time for.
card_roles.Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff: Two mana for two colours, and a busy table hands you Treasures — which spend on exactly the pips a five-colour activation wants. Cheap rungs are the whole game early.
card_roles.Mikaeus, the Lunarch: Cast him for X and he is a real threat; fetch him and X is zero, which is the one cold-start target this deck has never had adjudicated. Treat him as a card to cast, not a card to find.
card_roles.Mox Amber: Free, and it taps for any colour among your legendary creatures and planeswalkers — with Sisay out, that is at least one real pip. As a fetch target it is live at base power, but it adds no colour to the ladder.
card_roles.Najeela, the Blade-Blossom: The finisher, at three mana, so she comes off a Sisay with two colours behind her. Her untap costs the same five pips as the commander's activation, so the battery does double duty.
card_roles.Negate: One of the counterspells you keep for the turn you commit, aimed at removal and sweepers rather than at threats. Two mana is a fair price for keeping your whole ladder.
card_roles.Path to Exile: One white mana for the creature that has to die right now, at the cost of a basic for them. Save it for a commander or a combo piece, not for a beater.
card_roles.Raff Capashen, Ship's Mage: Every legend in your hand gains flash, so you deploy on their end step and untap with mana for an activation. Four mana that changes when you are allowed to build the ladder.
card_roles.Reki, the History of Kamigawa: A card for every legendary spell you cast from hand, which is most of this deck. Note the trigger wants a cast — the ones you fetch do not draw you anything.
card_roles.Relic of Legends: Three mana that turns any untapped legendary creature into a coloured pip, and it taps for one itself. Non-legendary, so it is another piece of fuel you have to draw.
card_roles.Rhystic Study: The best card in the deck that the tutor cannot see. Play it on a busy turn cycle and let the table decide whether to pay you or feed you.
card_roles.Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari: A two-mana blue rung that untaps whenever you cast a legendary spell and loots away the dead draws. Take it early for the colour, and forget the transform half unless the game stalls.
card_roles.Saffi Eriksdotter: Two mana for a green-white rung, and she trades herself to bring a creature back the turn it dies. Keep her sacrifice available on the turn you expect removal.
card_roles.Samut, Voice of Dissent: Five mana of red and green with flash, and the {W} untap gives the battery another tap. Everything you fetch afterwards can attack the turn it arrives.
card_roles.Seedborn Muse: Untap everything on every opponent's untap step: three extra windows a turn cycle to activate, protect, or both. Non-legendary and a Game Changer, so draw it and expect the table to react.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: One green mana and a tap for as many mana as your biggest creature's power, in any combination of colours — often the whole activation in one go. Get a fat body down first and she pays for everything.
card_roles.Shalai, Voice of Plenty: Hexproof for you and every other creature, which shuts off targeted removal for the whole ladder. She does not protect herself, so hold something for her.
card_roles.Sheoldred, the Apocalypse: Four mana that punishes every draw at the table and pays you for your own. Fetch her against the value decks; she also blocks anything that walks into deathtouch.
card_roles.Silence: One white mana, and no opponent casts a spell for the rest of the turn. Cast it before the activation you cannot afford to lose, not in response to their answer.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless mana that deploys her a turn early and pays nothing toward the five pips she then wants. Cast it, then go find colour.
card_roles.Surrak Dragonclaw: Five mana that makes himself and every creature spell you cast uncounterable, which is the answer to the blue seat. He is also a 6/6, which matters more than it looks in a deck of small legends.
card_roles.Swan Song: One blue for the counterspell that matters most, and the 2/2 flier you give away is a fair rate. Hold it for the enchantment-based lock or the combo instant.
card_roles.Teferi, Time Raveler: Opponents may only act at sorcery speed, so nothing interrupts an activation while he is out. Three mana, two colours on the ladder, and a bounce mode when a lock piece lands.
card_roles.Thalia, Heretic Cathar: Their creatures and their nonbasic lands arrive tapped, which is a full turn of tempo across three seats. Fetch her early, when a tempo tax compounds instead of a removal spell.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The reset, and it kills your ladder too, so aim it on a turn you are behind rather than a turn you are ahead. Pay only the X you need.
card_roles.Yoshimaru, Ever Faithful: One white mana, live as a fetch even at base power, and it grows on every legendary permanent that follows. The perfect turn-one play in a deck that wants a colour on board before the first activation.

mulligan:
Everyone mulligans this deck hunting for the commander. She is the one card you do not need to find — the model casts her by turn three in 95 games out of 100. Keep for the things she cannot go and get.

You have seen how the 99 splits: six cards can pay a five-pip activation and three of those six are non-legendary, so they only ever arrive by draw. That is the whole judgement in a keep. Fuel and colours, not payoffs.

Three things make a seven. Two to four lands including at least one source that makes any colour — Command Tower, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard, Forbidden Orchard, Plaza of Heroes, a fetch, or Secluded Courtyard on Human. Something that accelerates or pays: Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Relic of Legends. And best of all, a cheap multicolour legend, because that hand casts Sisay and immediately climbs.

An early accelerant shows up by turn six in 64 games out of 100. So a seven without one is not unlucky, it is under the curve you are expected to hit — ship it and draw a normal hand instead.

Ship the payoff hand. Jodah, Kenrith, Surrak and Samut with no fixing is four cards you cannot cast plus a 2/2 who can only find Mox Amber, Mikaeus or Yoshimaru. Ship the hand whose acceleration is Sol Ring and Delighted Halfling, because both deploy her a turn early and neither pays one pip of what she does next. Ship counterspells with one land — interaction is the half of this deck you can comfortably draw into later, and protection is already available by turn six in 80 games out of 100.

Count colours, not lands, when the hand is close. Your seven keeps itself on the land rule 84% of the time, so lands are rarely the question; four lands making three colours between them is a hand that casts your commander and then watches her.

Two sequencing habits to take into game one. Keep toward the ladder's second rung rather than toward a turn-three commander. And never activate into a cold board: land a colour-diverse legend first, because at power 2 your entire menu is Mox Amber, Mikaeus and Yoshimaru, and Mox Amber adds no colour at all.
upgrades:
Seven of the ten are legendary permanents, and in this deck that is a category with a price on it: 33 legendary permanents sit inside the tutor's reach and the other 26 nonland cards sit permanently outside it. A shortlist that ignores that split is a shortlist for someone else's deck.

The narrowest rung comes first. At base power 2 the gate is mana value under 2 and the list holds three legal targets, one of which adds no colour. Two of the ten are mana-value-0 legendary lands — Gaea's Cradle and Minamo, School at Water's Edge — in a 40-land base that runs none. One of them widens the cold-start menu by a third; both widen it by two thirds, out of the slot where that width is cheapest.

Adoption runs wide across the ten. Five sit inside EDHREC's top 700 — The One Ring at 92, Walking Ballista at 441, Gaea's Cradle at 448, Minamo at 601, Aggravated Assault at 698 — and the tail reaches Captain Sisay at 4,588 and Kethis, the Hidden Hand at 7,342. That tail is deck-shaped rather than unloved: a second repeatable legendary tutor and a graveyard rebuild answer holdings the audit counts at one and zero.

The bracket column reads 4 before and 4 after on all ten. Nothing here is a power-level decision wearing an upgrade's clothes.

The rejections carry as much information as the picks. Freed from the Real opens eight lines and is non-legendary, which is the blind spot again rather than a fix for it. Basalt Monolith makes colourless mana into a cost with zero generic in it. And every obsolescence-index replacement for Faeburrow Elder — Shang-Chi, Kami of Whispered Hopes, Mona Lisa, Frog Butler — fails the same one-line oracle read: none of them makes more than a single colour.
mana_base:
Forty lands, seventeen of them entering tapped. That is 42% against the one-in-three budget the builder allows itself, and it is the first figure in the audit. It reads as the invoice for a menu rather than as a mistake. Nine fetches, eight fixing lands and eight untapped duals is what buying {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} on demand costs you, and the tapped half is where the bill lands.

The interesting disagreement is between pip share and source share. White carries 38.3% of the deck's pips on 23.1% of its sources; red carries 8.0% of the pips on 18.5%. In most lists that is a misallocation. Here it is the design: the cost that runs the deck asks for one of each colour, so the base is levelled across five colours instead of tuned to the cast costs. Totals come out at 26 white, 27 green, 22 blue, 21 black and 21 red — a spread of six across the whole rainbow.

Black is the outlier, and one card explains it. On lands alone black lands on curve 29.9% of the time against 70 to 79% for everything else, because Dauthi Voidwalker's double-black cost is priced at turn two and pushes black's target to 36 sources where every other colour asks 22. Against 12 black lands in a 40-land deck, that target is a yardstick, not a possibility.

The ramp is what closes the gap: nine dorks, five rocks, a ritual and one land-ramp effect. Counted in, black rises to 61.0% and 21 sources, green to 95.1%, white to 94.4%, blue to 90.7% and red to 89.5%. The creature half of this mana base is not really acceleration — it is the fixing, which is why Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder read as load-bearing rather than as extra.

One accounting rule matters more here than anywhere else: only unconditional mana counts. Delighted Halfling and Unclaimed Territory make mana that cannot pay an activated ability at all, so they count as sources of nothing toward the deck's signature cost; Plaza of Heroes keeps one unrestricted coloured mode and Secluded Courtyard says "or activate an ability", so both do count. Raw mana crosses five on turn six, at a mean of 5.869 against 3.187 on turn three. After that your constraint is colour, never count.

combo_lines.002:
The clause this case turns on is CR 508.4: a creature put onto the battlefield attacking never "attacked" for trigger purposes. Najeela's own tokens cannot re-trigger her in the combat that made them, so the loop grows between combats, not inside one.

The rest is arithmetic. Every attacker but Derevi is a Warrior, so attackers run 3, 5, 9, 17 against a cost fixed at five mana, and Derevi's untap triggers equal the creatures that connect. Combat 1 is two triggers short and is paid from lands untapped beforehand. Combat 2 breaks even. Combat 3 runs away.

The holding: real, deterministic, unbounded — and not a two-card infinite. These two make no mana between them, and the record treats a base producing {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat as a requirement. One correction rides along: CR 118.3c, "activating mana abilities is not mandatory", puts the loop's life cost at zero.
